classification.difficultyReason: Derive the combined exponent in two reciprocal-power expansions and sum three signed contributions.

content.prompt: Find the coefficient of $x^{10}$ in the expansion of $$\left(x+\frac2x\right)^9\left(2x-\frac1x\right)^5.$$

answer.short:
$3248$.

The general-term exponent is $14-2k-2r$; use $k+r=2$ and sum the three cases.
answer.worked:
Multiplying the general terms gives
$$\begin{align*}T_{k,r}&=\binom9k x^{9-k}(2x^{-1})^k\binom5r(2x)^{5-r}(-x^{-1})^r\\T_{k,r}&=\binom9k\binom5r2^{k+5-r}(-1)^r x^{14-2k-2r}.\end{align*}$$
For $x^{10}$,
$$\begin{align*}14-2k-2r&=10\\k+r&=2.\end{align*}$$
The cases are $(k,r)=(2,0),(1,1),(0,2)$. Let $C_{10}$ be the coefficient of $x^{10}$.
$$\begin{align*}C_{10}&=\binom92\binom502^7-\binom91\binom512^5+\binom90\binom522^3\\C_{10}&=4608-1440+80\\C_{10}&=3248.\end{align*}$$
